World

Mon Nov 2global-institutions

UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara ends after 35 years as Security Council deadlocks

The UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara (MINURSO) stopped operating on Sunday after its mandate expired at midnight Saturday, when the Security Council failed to agree on renewing it, according to the UN, AP and NPR.

Mon Nov 2security

Ukraine and Russia say hackers hijacked their emergency alert apps to send fake nuclear warnings

Ukraine's Air Alert app sent false warnings of radiation, chemical attacks and street fighting late Sunday, and hours later Russia's emergencies ministry said its own warnings app had suffered a "massive cyberattack", according to the BBC, AP and AFP.

Mon Nov 2conflict

Israeli forces pull out of Hebron after operation launched over the killing of two soldiers

Israel's military said its soldiers withdrew on Monday from the area of its operation in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron, and Hebron Governor Khaled Dudin said Palestinian security forces had taken full control and displaced families could return, according to AFP, Al Jazeera and Anadolu Agency.

Mon Nov 2conflict

Saudi-led coalition says it shot down a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at southern Saudi Arabia

Coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki said on Monday that air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile the Houthis launched toward Saudi Arabia's southern region, according to the official Saudi Press Agency, Al Jazeera and TRT World.

Mon Nov 2disaster

Spain identifies 66 of 69 train crash victims, including four Americans

Authorities said 54 of the identified victims of last week's high-speed train collision near Urda, in Toledo province, were Spanish and 12 were foreign nationals, according to RTVE, AFP and AP.

Sun Nov 1diplomacy

Iran holds third day of talks with Qatari mediators on ending war with US

Iranian negotiators were in Doha on Sunday for a third consecutive day of talks with Qatari mediators aimed at a deal to end the US-Israeli war on Iran, an official briefed on the discussions told Reuters.

Sun Nov 1conflict

Russian strikes cut power to hundreds of thousands in Ukraine as Oleshky truce ends

Russian strikes on energy infrastructure left hundreds of thousands of Ukrainian households without power on Sunday, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said.

Sun Nov 1elections

Bulgaria's acting president Iotova wins runoff, early results show

Acting President Iliana Iotova is the apparent winner of Bulgaria's presidential runoff, initial results showed on Sunday, and her rival Andrey Gyurov conceded defeat, AP reported.

Sun Nov 1public-safety

More than 100 police injured as Gen Z protests turn to rioting in Frankfurt

Rioters damaged 17 stores in Frankfurt, five of which were looted, and more than 100 police officers were injured, Hesse state interior minister Roman Poseck said on Sunday.

Sat Oct 31conflict

US approves $2.1 billion sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine

The US State Department approved a proposed sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 MSE interceptor missiles to Ukraine, estimated at $2.1 billion and paid for with European and Canadian funding.

Sat Oct 31conflict

Iran's Revolutionary Guards say four tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said four oil tankers, including a supertanker carrying more than 2 million barrels of crude, struck mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday.

Sat Oct 31courts

Poland's constitutional court standoff escalates after its president is suspended

Government-appointed judges suspended the contested president of Poland's Constitutional Tribunal, Bogdan Święczkowski, prompting President Karol Nawrocki to cut short a foreign trip and accuse the government of seizing the court by force.

Sat Oct 31global-institutions

UN biodiversity talks in Yerevan end with plan to speed up nature targets

Countries at the COP17 UN biodiversity conference in Yerevan, Armenia, adopted the "Yerevan Pathway" on Saturday after roughly 12 hours of overnight negotiations, aiming to speed up work toward 2030 goals to halt nature loss.

Fri Oct 30elections

Final count confirms Israel deadlock: Netanyahu bloc 53 seats, Eisenkot bloc 48, Arab-led parties 19

Israel's Central Elections Committee published final results early Friday showing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc with 53 of the Knesset's 120 seats, the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot with 48 and Arab-led parties with 19, leaving no side with the 61 needed to govern, according to The Times of Israel, AP and Ynet.

Fri Oct 30conflict

Russian drone strike on Dnipro train station kills at least 14, Ukrainian officials say

At least 14 people were killed and at least 14 wounded on Thursday when a Russian jet-powered drone hit a crowded platform at the main railway station in Dnipro, Ukrainian officials said, according to the BBC, DW and CBS News.

Fri Oct 30conflict

Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh; Houthis deny targeting Mecca region

The Saudi-led coalition said Saudi air defenses destroyed two Houthi ballistic missiles fired toward Riyadh on Thursday and a drone over the Mecca region on Friday, while the Houthis denied launching any attack on Friday, according to Reuters, via Al-Monitor, Al Arabiya and Xinhua.

Fri Oct 30diplomacy

EU-Canada summit opens in Montreal as 'associate member' wording is dropped from draft declaration

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen pushed for closer ties at a two-day summit in Montreal, after a draft joint declaration replaced the idea of Canada becoming an EU 'associate member' with a pledge of 'ever closer association,' according to Reuters, via France 24, CBC News and AP.

Fri Oct 30disaster

Italian helicopter with EU force crashes in Bosnia, killing four

An Italian CH-47 Chinook helicopter serving with the EU's EUFOR mission crashed during routine training near Brčko in northern Bosnia and Herzegovina on Thursday, killing four personnel and injuring 11, EUFOR said.

Thu Oct 29disaster

Spain train crash death toll reaches 68 as minister blames 'inexplicable' control-centre order

At least 68 people were killed when a high-speed Renfe train struck a stationary Iryo train near Urda in central Spain on Wednesday, and Transport Minister Óscar Puente said a control-centre decision to let the train resume at normal speed is at the centre of the investigation, according to the BBC, The Guardian and Euronews.

Thu Oct 29conflict

Moscow mayor says 613 drones flew toward the Russian capital overnight

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 613 drones flew toward the Moscow region between Wednesday evening and Thursday morning, with 231 destroyed on approach to the city and most of the rest neutralized farther out, according to Reuters, via Al Jazeera, and Meduza.

Thu Oct 29elections

Flávio Bolsonaro lands in Miami and says he did not flee Brazil

Brazil's defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro arrived in the Miami area on Wednesday after Brazil cancelled his passports in a criminal investigation, and said in a statement that he "did not flee Brazil," according to the BBC and The Guardian.

Thu Oct 29conflict

El Salvador sends more than 2,000 troops to Haiti to find four missing soldiers as Haiti delays its elections

El Salvador's foreign ministry said Wednesday it is deploying more than 2,000 soldiers to Haiti to search for four Salvadoran air force technicians missing since an Oct. 18 ambush and to help fight gangs, according to the BBC and Al Jazeera.

Thu Oct 29diplomacy

Ethiopia says it has received Russian Su-35 fighter jets as fighting continues in Tigray

Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed said Wednesday that his country has received Su-35 fighter jets from Russia and plans to acquire four S-400 air defence systems, as government forces fight in the northern Tigray region, according to the BBC and Al Jazeera.

Wed Oct 28elections

Netanyahu's Likud leads Israel's vote count, but neither camp has a clear path to a majority

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud was on course to be the largest party after Tuesday's Israeli election, but neither his bloc nor Gadi Eisenkot's opposition camp had a clear route to a 61-seat majority, according to the BBC and The Guardian.

Wed Oct 28public-safety

Two high-speed trains collide in central Spain, halting the Madrid-Andalusia line

Two high-speed passenger trains, one run by Renfe and one by Iryo, collided near Urda in Spain's Toledo province on Wednesday morning, and rail infrastructure manager Adif suspended high-speed service between Madrid and Andalusia.

Wed Oct 28conflict

Oleshky truce widened across Kherson region as Finland and Norway leaders hold rare call with Putin

A local ceasefire that began Tuesday around the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky has been extended across the wider Kherson region to give humanitarian convoys safe passage, U.S. first lady Melania Trump and Ukrainian officials said.

Wed Oct 28diplomacy

U.S. to grant visas to Flávio Bolsonaro as reports say he left Brazil despite court order

A senior U.S. State Department official said Tuesday that Brazil's defeated presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro and his family will be granted U.S. visas, as several outlets reported he had left Brazil despite a Supreme Court order to surrender his passports.

Wed Oct 28courts

Egyptian court orders closure of independent news site Mada Masr and fines its editor

A Cairo court on Tuesday convicted Lina Attalah, editor-in-chief of the independent Egyptian news site Mada Masr, of running a website without a license, fined her 3 million Egyptian pounds and ordered the outlet closed, according to Mada Masr, the AP and the BBC.

Tue Oct 27elections

Israelis vote in first election since Oct. 7 attack as Netanyahu faces Eisenkot challenge

Polls opened in Israel on Tuesday for the first national election since the Hamas-led attack of Oct. 7, 2023, with surveys showing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a tight race with former military chief Gadi Eisenkot.

Tue Oct 27conflict

Local truce takes hold in occupied Oleshky as Russia strikes Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities

A limited ceasefire brokered by US first lady Melania Trump began on Tuesday in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky to allow aid deliveries and evacuations, while Ukraine said Russia launched 16 ballistic missiles and more than 280 drones elsewhere overnight.

Friday · Oct 23, 2026 · World Digest · conflict

Russia fires 21 ballistic missiles at Kyiv hours after agreeing to resume talks
